newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Blast near Turkish mission in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Blast near Turkish mission in Australia.

text.p: An explosion destroyed a house next to the Turkish consulate-general in Sydney on Sunday, but there were no immediate reports of serious injuries, police said.
Police said two men were seen running from the scene just before the blast and the Special Squad, used in sensitive cases, had been called in.
"Two men were seen running away from the scene before the explosion," police told reporters at the scene in the upscale Sydney suburb of Woollahra, home to several foreign missions.
The consul-general was not in the mission at the time of the blast, police said.

A police spokesman told Reuters the explosion occurred just before 5.00 p.m. local time (0600 GMT), destroying a vacant two-storey house next to the consulate and damaging surrounding homes in the eastern Sydney Suburb.
Debris was blasted up to 100 metres (110 yards) away and the explosion was heard about five km (three miles) away.
The police spokesman would not comment on the cause of the blast but a policeman at the scene ruled out a gas explosion.
"It would appear to be some sort of explosion, but not a gas explosion," senior constable Scott Willis told a Reuters journalist at the scene.
Willis said the blast may have been caused by a bomb, but said police were not certain if the explosion was politically motivated or if the Turkish consulate was the target.
One person was taken to hospital suffering from smoke inhalation.
Turkish officials were not immediately available for comment.
In 1980, the Turkish consul-general in Sydney and a bodyguard were shot dead in the city. A group called the Justice Commandos of the Armenian Genocide claimed responsibility.
